Design and implement a shared per-reconcile-pass cache (or equivalent) for findResidueDuplicate's gh issue list call, scoped correctly across every call site active in one reconcile pass.

A single reconcile pass touching N stuck dirs/paths makes at most one gh issue list --limit 10000 call for a given repo, not N.

No change to which duplicates are detected or how dedup-hit/append/reopen decisions are made.

Cache is correctly scoped to one reconcile pass (no stale cross-pass reuse).

Title: flow Step 2.8 claim-write did not land for #2322's build/test dispatch — verify claiming actually fires
Type: bug

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

## Origin

Origin: reflect light from #2322
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow`'s Step 2.8 documents that a record reference run with `build`/`test` in the
resolved step list claims its targets via `bin/claim-targets.js` before the pipeline proper
starts, writing `claims/issue-{n}.json` on the `claims-registry` branch. For record #2322 (this
run's own worktree, `worktree-record-2322`, PR #2483), the earlier `/flow #2322` call ran
`build,test` and completed both successfully (commits `5abbceffa..72c61d3b8`, PR opened and
pushed). At wrap-up time for the `review,polish,wrap-up` follow-up call, a direct check of the
claims registry found no `claims/issue-2322.json` blob was ever written — `gh api
repos/thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks/contents/claims/issue-2322.json?ref=claims-registry` returns
404, and `gh api repos/.../commits?path=claims/issue-2322.json&sha=claims-registry` returns an
empty array (no commit in that path's history at all). The issue also carries no `bot:in-progress`
label. No harm resulted this run — the same session held the worktree continuously and no
competing agent contended for the record — but the absence means the cross-agent claim-lock
protocol documented for `/flow`'s Step 2.8 did not actually fire (or fired and was silently
dropped) for this dispatch path.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Reproduce a `/flow #{n}` invocation with `build,test` in the resolved step list against a
      fresh record and confirm whether `bin/claim-targets.js` is actually invoked at Step 2.8
- [ ] If it is invoked but the write silently fails (e.g. a skip-guard condition matching
      unexpectedly, or a swallowed error from `claim-store.js`), fix the gap and add a regression
      test pinning that a `build`/`test` step-list run always produces a live claim blob
      immediately after Step 2.8 passes
- [ ] If claiming is intentionally skipped for this dispatch shape (e.g. a direct `/flow` call
      that isn't `/dispatch`-originated), confirm that's documented and that the "already-claimed"
      framing other skills assume (e.g. a follow-up `review,polish,wrap-up` call being told the
      group is "already-claimed") doesn't silently rely on a claim that was never actually written

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `/flow #{n}` run with `build` or `test` in its step list either (a) demonstrably writes a
      live `claims/issue-{n}.json` blob before Step 4 begins, confirmed by a fresh `gh api` read,
      or (b) the skip condition it took is named and intentional, with no follow-on skill treating
      a never-claimed record as if a claim exists

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

## Suggested resolution

Investigate `bin/claim-targets.js` / `bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`'s invocation from
`flow/claim-targets.md`'s Step 2.8 skip-guard list against this exact dispatch shape (a
dispatcher-minted, non-empty `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` handed to `/flow #{n}` directly) to see whether one
of the documented skip conditions unexpectedly matched.

## Decision-log reference

STAGED — Step 3: tangential idea "flow Step 2.8 claim-write did not land for #2322" — backlog
candidate — landing: born-ready (defer-reason: tangential). Surface at the Queue writes gate.

Origin: filed by the docs-health curation row (`/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`, D1 restructural), during #2322's wrap-up.

## Current State

`docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/` inventory paragraph states: "Both destructive branch checks read it screen-then-confirm: archive-branches and prune-remote screen the in-scope set in one bulk call and re-read per-branch only to confirm a destructive provisional verdict."

This is no longer accurate for `archive-branches.js`. Since #2252 (and widened by #2322), a MERGED-screened or screen-null non-cherry-equivalent branch reaches the per-branch confirm even when its provisional verdict is a non-destructive `skip` — the confirm's own squash-provenance evidence, not the provisional verdict, decides whether the branch is actually destructive. The claim stays true for `prune-remote.js`, whose provisional `skip` still short-circuits before any confirm call.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Update the sentence in `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s reconcile inventory paragraph so it states the current, differing behavior of the two checks: `prune-remote.js`'s provisional skip still short-circuits (confirm only follows a destructive provisional), while `archive-branches.js`'s confirm now also runs for a MERGED- or screen-null-screened, non-cherry-equivalent branch regardless of whether the provisional itself is destructive (`squashCandidate` routing, #2252/#2322) — the confirm's own evidence, not the provisional, has the final say for that check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sentence no longer claims both checks re-read per-branch "only to confirm a destructive provisional verdict" — it distinguishes the two checks' actual routing conditions, cross-referencing `docs/reconcile-checks.md`'s Merged-proof / Confirm-routing symmetry sections rather than restating their detail inline.

_Filed by `wrap-up`'s docs curation row via the docs-health issue-filing convention._

Origin: reflect full mode from #2324 (wrap-up)

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

During record #2324's `/test` phase, `node bin/verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch main` was run from a worktree checkout to check for frontend/UI files in the diff. It returned `{base: <current worktree HEAD>, files: []}` — a base identical to HEAD, with an empty changed-file list — silently (exit 0), even though the worktree branch was well ahead of `main`. The result looked plausible enough (valid JSON, no error) that it could easily be trusted at face value; it was caught only by an independent cross-check via `git diff --name-only` against the known-good merge-base. `/claude-tweaks:review`'s own Step 2 documents the underlying hazard generally ("never trust a bare local branch name for `{base}` — a long-lived worktree's local tracking branch routinely drifts behind its remote"), but this specific CLI's `--changed-files --integration-branch` handling doesn't appear to apply that `origin/{base}` resolution rule, and returns no signal when its resolved base ends up suspiciously identical to HEAD.

## Deliverables

Read `bin/verify.js`'s `--changed-files --integration-branch <ref>` implementation and confirm whether it resolves `<ref>` via `origin/<ref>` (per review's own documented hazard) or a bare local branch name when invoked from inside a worktree.

If it resolves a bare local branch: fix it to resolve via `origin/<ref>` first, matching the rule `/claude-tweaks:review`'s Step 2 already documents for hand-written git commands.

Regardless of the root cause found: add a guard that surfaces a warning (or a distinct result field) when the resolved `base` equals `HEAD` in a context where the caller's own worktree branch is known to be ahead of `main` — so a caller doesn't have to independently cross-check via `git diff` to catch a silently degenerate result.

## Acceptance Criteria

A regression test reproducing this repo's own #2324-review scenario (a worktree branch ahead of `origin/main`, `--changed-files --integration-branch main` invoked from inside the worktree) resolves a non-empty `files` list matching the branch's real diff, not an empty list.

`node --test tests/bin-lib/verify*.test.js` (or wherever the existing suite for this CLI lives) passes with the new regression test included.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

Origin: wrap-up of #2319

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `acceptance-labeling` check (registered ~line 450) unconditionally expects a `demo:pending` label on every resolved issue number, reporting `fail: #{n}: missing demo:pending label` when it's absent. It has no knowledge of `verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate, which legitimately skips Steps 1-4 (no `demo:pending` bootstrap) for a record whose `risk`/`size` facets don't clear the resolved `risk-floor`/`size-floor` (e.g. `risk:low` x `size:low` against the default `risk-floor: high`/`size-floor: high`) — an explicitly documented 'not required' outcome, not an error state, per that file's own text ('The record closes with no `demo:*` label and no ceremony ... It stays demoable later on request').

Observed live on run `2026-09-14T194928-record-2319` (record #2319, `risk:low` x `size:low`): `exceedsOversightFloor` correctly returned `{exceeds: false}`, Steps 1-4 were correctly skipped, and `wrap-up-engine.js verify` then reported `acceptance-labeling: fail — #2319: missing demo:pending label` — a false positive on the exact path the gate exists to support.

## Deliverables

Teach the `acceptance-labeling` verify check to recognize the Oversight-floor skip as a passing (or explicitly-skipped) state rather than a failure — e.g. by re-running (or reading a recorded result of) `exceedsOversightFloor` for each resolved issue's `risk`/`size` facets before asserting the label must be present, and reporting `skip: "below oversight floor — demo:pending not required"` when it returns `exceeds: false`.

## Acceptance Criteria

A record whose facets fail to clear the resolved risk/size floor no longer fails `wrap-up-engine.js verify`'s `acceptance-labeling` check for lacking `demo:pending`. A record that does clear the floor and still lacks the label continues to fail exactly as before. A test in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/` pins both branches.

## Current State

Between cli-v3.6.0 and cli-v4.0.0, pbakaus/impeccable's CLI engine was rewritten from JavaScript (shipped inline in the npm package, under cli/engine/) to Rust (crates/ in the upstream repo), compiled to a per-platform binary. The npm package (impeccable@4.1.0) is now a thin shim (cli/bin/cli.js, ~95 lines) that locates or downloads the actual engine binary — from an optionalDependency package (@impeccable/cli-<os>-<arch>) or a checksum-verified download from GitHub releases, cached at ~/.impeccable/bin/<engine-version>/ — where <engine-version> is a SEPARATE version scheme (engine-v0.1.5 observed) decoupled from the npm package's own version (4.1.0) that `impeccable --version` reports.

This was discovered while re-pinning tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml's impeccable-cli entry from 3.6.0 to 4.1.0 (#2314) — the two behavioral claims impeccable-cli.md made about the old JS engine (findings-to-stdout, empty-array-on-clean-scan) are still true at 4.1.0 (verified against the new Rust source, crates/detect/src/cli.rs at cli-v4.1.0), but the manifest's static-assertion mechanism can no longer check them at all, since there is no local text source left to grep — only fixtures (real detect executions) can verify behavior against this artifact going forward.

## Deliverables

Read plugin/skills/design-wrapper/impeccable-cli.md in full against the new shim/binary architecture and judge whether it needs new content: does the wrapper need to document or handle a download failure, a checksum mismatch, an unsupported platform (no matching @impeccable/cli-<os>-<arch> package and no cached/downloadable binary), or the IMPECCABLE_BIN/IMPECCABLE_HOME/IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE env var overrides the shim now supports? None of these failure modes existed under the old inline-JS architecture, and the wrapper doc was written entirely against that architecture.

Decide whether tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml's impeccable-cli entry needs a new fixture (or a documented accepted gap) covering an engine-download failure, given the existing two fixtures only exercise the happy path.

## Acceptance Criteria

A decision is recorded (either "no new content needed, out of scope because X" or a concrete new section added to impeccable-cli.md) for each failure mode named above.

If a new fixture is added, it passes against the installed 4.1.0 binary.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`reflect/SKILL.md`'s Auto mode routing table sends a reflect finding to one of four destinations
by category (Safety regression / Convention drift / Tangential idea / Pattern observation), and
the file is explicit that only `Category: tangential` becomes a Queue-writes record proposal —
"omitted for `convention`/`observation` findings (those are never Queue writes)." But
`bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `SECTION_MAP` classifies staged files by filename prefix alone:
`/^(reflect|digest-promotion|leftover|...)(-|\b)/` routes every `reflect-*.md` file into
`SECTIONS.QUEUE`, with no read of the file's own `**Category:**` field. `SECTION_STANCES[QUEUE]`
resolves to `apply`, and the "On approval" step for a `Q#` item is "create the record — reading
`Title:`/`Type:`/`Labels:` and the body from the item's staged file" — fields a non-tangential
reflect finding's staged file never carries, by the same SKILL.md's own contract.

Reproduced live in this run (`2026-09-14T182541-record-1800`, wrap-up for #1800):
`staged/reflect-1.md` is a `Category: observation` finding (no Title:/Type:/Labels: header, per
contract) with `**Files:** general (test suite infrastructure)`. `console-resolve.js --policy
console-auto` classified it into "Queue writes" and resolved it `AUTO-RESOLVED: apply` — the same
resolution a genuine tangential idea gets. Executing that resolution literally would attempt
`gh issue create` against a file with no `Title:`/`Type:`/`Labels:` fields to read, either
erroring or filing a malformed issue with fields guessed from the wrong shape.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `classifyStagedItem` (or its caller) reads the staged file's `**Category:**` field for any
      `reflect-*`/`digest-promotion-*`/`leftover-*` (any prefix in the same `SECTION_MAP` bucket
      that reflect's own contract distinguishes by category) match, and routes non-tangential
      categories to a section whose stance doesn't attempt record creation — most naturally
      `SECTIONS.PENDING` (the same "surface for a human, no auto-file" treatment `review-*`
      findings already get), not `SECTIONS.QUEUE`.
- [ ] A regression test pinning that a `Category: observation`/`Category: convention` staged
      reflect file resolves to something other than `apply`-as-Queue-write, alongside an existing
      `Category: tangential` file still resolving to `apply`-as-Queue-write as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `console-resolve.js --policy console-auto` on a fixture `staged/reflect-N.md` carrying
   `**Category:** observation` and no `Title:`/`Type:`/`Labels:` header does not classify it into
   "Queue writes" / resolution `apply`.
2. The same CLI on a fixture `staged/reflect-N.md` carrying `**Category:** tangential` and a
   `Title:`/`Type:`/`Labels:` header still classifies it into "Queue writes" / resolution `apply`,
   unchanged from today.
3. `npm test` green.

## Original request

Origin: reflect full mode (Near-misses lens, meta-finding on the mechanism itself) from
`/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Phase 4 Review Console step, dispatch run
`2026-09-14T182541-record-1800` (#1800's own wrap-up).

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`
— all three confirmed still true at this shaping pass:

- **Read-back race** (~line 400): post-write verification (#2073) re-reads immediately with no
  retry/backoff (`if (!verifyClaimLanded(deps, repoSlug, issue, opts.runId, knownTip))`). On the
  contents-API transport `knownTip` is `null`, so the read-back hits GitHub's
  eventually-consistent contents API and can legitimately return the pre-write blob — a spurious
  exit 5 on a claim that actually landed. The file's own header already warns against
  eventually-consistent GitHub reads elsewhere.
- **Claim leak on abort** (~line 227, confirmed): `abort()` releases only `claimedThisRun`
  (`releaseClaimedThisRun(deps, repoSlug, opts.runId, claimedThisRun)`). `stopOrSkip(issue,
  'unverified', 'unverified', 5, {})` runs (confirmed, ~line 401) *before* the target is pushed
  onto `claimedThisRun` (the `claimedThisRun.push(issue)` call is one line after the verification
  check), so a target whose claim genuinely landed (just couldn't be verified back) leaks until
  TTL expiry with no `bot:in-progress` marker making it visible.
- **Stale doc comment** (~line 225, confirmed): `abort()`'s comment still enumerates only exit
  codes 3 and 4 ("`exitCode` is 3 for a `contested`/`inFlight` envelope, 4 for a `transient`
  one") — exit 5 (`unverified`) was added without updating it.

## Deliverables

- Add a bounded retry/backoff to the post-write read-back verification when `knownTip` is `null`,
  before declaring exit 5.
- Release (or otherwise make visible) the `unverified` target's claim on abort, not just
  `claimedThisRun`.
- Update `abort()`'s doc comment to include exit 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A simulated eventually-consistent stale read on the contents-API path no longer produces a
  spurious exit 5 within the retry window.
- An aborted run with an `unverified` target leaves that claim in a state a later run can
  detect/reclaim before TTL, not silently leaked.
- `abort()`'s doc comment lists exit codes 3, 4, and 5.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

For the read-back race: wrap the `verifyClaimLanded` call (~line 400) in a small bounded
retry loop (a few attempts with a short backoff) specifically for the `knownTip === null` case —
the git-CAS path (`knownTip` set) already has a real tip to compare against and doesn't need
this, since a git-CAS success is immediately consistent. Only declare exit 5 after the retry
window is exhausted. For the claim leak: capture the `unverified` issue's claim state (the
context `verifyClaimLanded` already had before failing) and pass it to `abort()` so it can be
released or explicitly flagged alongside `claimedThisRun`'s own release — the goal is that a
genuinely-landed-but-unverified claim doesn't sit invisible until TTL; releasing it (so a later
run can pick it up cleanly) is the safer default over leaving it silently held. Update the
`abort()` doc comment in the same change.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js` — the read-back retry (~line 400), the claim
  leak fix (~line 227, `abort()` and the `unverified` stop path), and the doc comment update

## Gotchas

- The retry must be scoped to the `knownTip === null` (contents-API) path only — the git-CAS
  path's `knownTip`-based verification is already immediately consistent and doesn't need
  (or benefit from) a retry; adding one there would just slow down every claim for no
  correctness gain.
- Releasing an `unverified` claim on abort must not race with the claim that write actually
  produced — verify the release targets the same claim identity (`repoSlug`, `issue`, `opts.runId`)
  the write itself used, so a genuinely different run's claim on the same issue is never touched.

`dispatch/mcp-transport.md` already documents, as an accepted gap, that `bin/resolve-linked-prs.js`
(the #1224 open-linked-PR exclusion) has no confirmed MCP mapping and fails open (no exclusions)
when `gh` is absent. This run hit that gap for real, not hypothetically: of the 27 candidates in
the eligible queue, record #1594 already had an open PR (#1908, "Fixes #1594") that the automated
check could not detect on this transport. It was caught only because the dispatching session
independently ran a manual, targeted subagent scan of open PR bodies/titles for closing-keyword
references before finalizing the group selection — a step the documented protocol does not
actually specify or require anywhere. Without that improvised check, #1594 could have been
re-dispatched to a second build in parallel with the already-open PR #1908, producing conflicting
work on the same record.

## Deliverables

      equivalent of `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, or an open-PR title/body scan folded
      directly into `queue-pull-script.md`'s MCP branch) rather than leaving it "accepted for now"
      indefinitely.
- [ ] Until a real mapping exists, consider making the manual verification this run improvised a
      documented, required step in `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s Step 2 section for the `gh`-absent
      path, so a future firing doesn't have to independently rediscover the same gap and the same
      workaround.

## Acceptance Criteria

   promoted from this run's improvisation to a documented, required step for the `gh`-absent

## Current State

Record #1302 built the WEBHOOK-TRIGGER mode (`plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`), the `webhook_triggers` schema field, the filter grammar, and both preconditions -- all documented from `create_webhook_trigger`'s own tool description, since `RemoteTrigger` was confirmed unavailable via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in that build session. This is the 4th consecutive session (2026-08-23 x2, 2026-08-26, 2026-09-05) to confirm the same unavailability. AC2 ("verified against a real (or explicitly documented dry-run) call") remains unmet: the request/response shape has never actually been confirmed against a live `create_webhook_trigger` call.

A prior follow-up for this same gap, #1485, was filed and closed on 2026-08-31 -- but the closing commit (`e0d4aded`, "[fast-lane] Dispatch-queue, worktree-guard, reconcile, and process-hygiene fixes (19 records)") bundled 19 unrelated record numbers via `Fixes #N` and contains no work touching `webhook-trigger.md`, `RemoteTrigger`, or live-call verification. #1485 appears to have been swept into an unrelated batch closure rather than substantively resolved -- its own acceptance criterion (a live or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call) was never actually satisfied. This record exists so the gap is not lost a second time to the same failure mode; whoever picks this up should close it only against real evidence of a live (or explicit dry-run) call, not a batch commit that doesn't mention the file.

## Deliverables

- Re-run `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in a session where the tool may be reachable -- 4 consecutive interactive-session misses is a strong signal worth testing in a different session type (cloud/routine) if one becomes available.
- Once reachable, call `create_webhook_trigger` against a real (or an explicit, logged dry-run) routine and record its actual required fields, response shape, and any App-not-installed error text.
- Diff the actual response against what `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` currently documents (Step 5's assembled body, the `routine_trigger_id` field, the App-not-installed error detection) and correct any mismatch.
- Before closing, verify the closing commit/PR actually touches `webhook-trigger.md` or names the live-verification evidence directly -- do not let this close via an unrelated batch sweep the way #1485 did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A live (or explicit dry-run) `create_webhook_trigger` call has been made and its actual request/response shape is confirmed to match (or has been corrected to match) `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`.
- The closing commit or PR description names this evidence directly (a transcript excerpt, a diff to `webhook-trigger.md`, or an explicit "confirmed matching, no changes needed" note) rather than a bare `Fixes #N` in an unrelated batch.

## Technical Approach

Start with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in whichever session type is available at build time. If reachable, make one real or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call and capture its actual request/response shape verbatim before touching the docs. Then diff that captured shape against `webhook-trigger.md`'s current documentation section by section (assembled body, `routine_trigger_id`, App-not-installed error detection) and correct only what actually differs.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` -- the documented request/response shape to verify and correct

## Gotchas

- If `RemoteTrigger`/`create_webhook_trigger` is still unreachable in whatever session builds this record, do not fabricate a "verified" result and do not close this record -- report the continued unavailability plainly (a 5th consecutive miss is itself a useful data point) and leave it open.
- Do not let this close via a bulk/batch commit that references this issue number without actually touching the files above -- that is exactly how #1485 was lost.

## Current State

Record #649 added `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s fan-out single-assistant-message-rule
sentence and per-site citations (AC1, fully test-pinned in `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`,
18/18 passing). AC2 — "A `/specify` red-team over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues launches its
personas in ≤ (number of sub-issues) assistant messages, verified in the transcript by `Agent`
tool_use blocks sharing a message id" — is a live-behavior criterion that cannot be verified by a
static `node --test` assertion; it can only be confirmed by observing an actual future `/specify`
decomposition run's transcript.

## Deliverables

Confirm, at the next `/specify` decomposition run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues, that
persona dispatch actually batches into ≤N assistant messages per `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s
fan-out single-assistant-message rule and `red-team.md`'s per-sub-issue batching unit. Record the
observation (transcript excerpt or note) against this item, or file a defect against
`red-team.md`'s dispatch prose if it does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

A `/specify` run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues is observed; its persona `Agent` tool_use
calls are confirmed (via transcript `tool_use` block message-id grouping) to arrive in ≤ (number of
sub-issues) assistant messages.

## Technical Approach

Wait for (or trigger) a `/claude-tweaks:specify` decomposition-mode run that produces 2 or more
`ceremony:standard` sub-issue records — `ceremony-check` (`assess-agent-autonomy/ceremony-check.md`)
resolves the tier per sub-issue during that run's own Step 3, so the tier isn't knowable until the
run happens. Once such a run occurs, inspect that session's stored transcript for the Step 5
red-team dispatch (`specify/red-team.md`'s Parallel dispatch section): locate the `Agent` tool_use
blocks for each dispatched persona and group them by the assistant message id each block belongs
to. Confirm the number of distinct assistant message ids covering all persona dispatches for a
given sub-issue is ≤ the number of sub-issues in that batch. Use the same read-only transcript
inspection method `transcript-payload-verification` documents for reading this session's own

Surface: backend

## Current State
`captureDebugPayload` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js:1633`) is env-gated (`CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE`) diagnostic instrumentation wired directly into `run()` — the general hook dispatcher invoked on every covered tool call — added by #1501 to chase a repro-resistant #989 investigation. #1501's own investigation found the actual cause without it (a fresh worktree's `@{u}` inherited `origin/main`), and #1860/PR #1874 (merged 2026-09-05) fixed `hasNoUpstreamYet` for that case with regression tests covering the inherited-upstream shape. The harness gap the instrumentation was added to diagnose is closed at the test level. Nothing in the repo reads the capture file, and no other open record cites `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE`. A maintainer has decided (this record's own resolution, 2026-09-13) to remove the instrumentation rather than keep it as permanent tooling.

## Deliverables
- Remove `captureDebugPayload(ctx)` (function definition, its header comment block, and its call site in `run()`) from `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`.
- Remove the three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests and their preceding comment block from `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `captureDebugPayload`'s function definition, its header comment (the `#1501: env-gated debug capture...` block), and its `captureDebugPayload(ctx);` call inside `run()` no longer exist in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`.
- [ ] The three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests (`unset by default, no file is written`; `when set, appends one JSON line per call...`; `an unwritable target never breaks the real gate call`) and their preceding `#1501` comment no longer exist in `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`.
- [ ] `grep -rn "captureDebugPayload\|CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE" plugin/ tests/` returns no results.
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach
Delete the `captureDebugPayload` function (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`, currently ~lines 1621-1646 including its header comment) and its call site inside `run()` (currently the `captureDebugPayload(ctx);` statement at the top of `run()`, ~line 1649) — `run()`'s remaining body is unaffected; it already builds `indeterminateTargets`/`warnings` and calls `runInner` immediately after.

Delete the corresponding test block in `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` (currently ~lines 1127-1176: the `#1501` comment plus all three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests) — the surrounding tests (the preceding block and the following `#1967` git-stash test) are unaffected and need no renumbering.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — remove `captureDebugPayload` function, its header comment, and its call in `run()`
- `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` — remove the three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests and their preceding comment

## Gotchas
- `run()` calls `captureDebugPayload(ctx)` unconditionally as its first statement — confirmed only one call site and one definition exist in the repo (`grep -rn "captureDebugPayload\|CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE"` against `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` and `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`) before removing either.
- Pure removal with no behavior change for any caller — `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` was already a no-op unless the env var was explicitly set for a deliberate capture session, so no production behavior depends on it.

## Original request

pre-tool-use.js: captureDebugPayload is permanent scaffolding in the production hook dispatcher

## Current State
`captureDebugPayload` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`, ~line 1409) — permanent, env-gated (`CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE`) diagnostic instrumentation added to chase one repro-resistant #989 bug — is wired directly into `run()`, the general hook dispatcher invoked on every covered tool call, rather than the actual ctx-field gap (between synthetic test payloads and live invocations) being closed in the test harness. Low runtime cost when unset, but sets a precedent for future "repro doesn't match" investigations to keep accumulating env-gated capture hooks in the production dispatcher rather than fixing the harness gap that necessitated it.

## Deliverables
Either (a) close the actual ctx-field gap in the test harness so synthetic payloads match live invocations and remove `captureDebugPayload` from `run()`, or (b) make a deliberate call to keep it as permanent tooling and document why in place of the current "added to chase one bug" framing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision is made and recorded: remove captureDebugPayload (harness gap closed) or keep it deliberately (comment updated to reflect permanent-tooling intent).
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision — whether to invest in closing the harness gap vs. keep the instrumentation is a product/maintainer call, not a mechanical fix; found by the pre-v6.112.0 whole-branch review.
